title: Coordinate-normalized additive cohomology pullback comparison
statement: Let $k\to k'$ be an algebra map of commutative rings. Let $C$ be a quasi-compact scheme with a separated map $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $h$ display $C'$ as its cartesian base change with projections $j:C'\to C$ and $f':C'\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-base-change]. Let $n\ge0$, let $G,G'$ be abelian sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], with additive coordinates $a_U:G(U)\simeq\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ and $a'_V:G'(V)\simeq\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ natural under every etale restriction. Let $q:j^*G\to G'$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] have adjoint section map given by structural pullback in these coordinates. Write $M=\mathcal O_C$ as the unit module and $M_{k'}$ for its canonical module pullback; write $HOver(f,M,n)$ with the structural scalar actions and $B=H.baseChangeLinear(f,M,n)$ for the untensored map [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison]. Use the Ext cohomology and its canonical etale pullback $j_H^*$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. There exist additive equivalences $e:H^n(G)\simeq HOver(f,M,n)$ and $e':H^n(G')\simeq HOver(f_{k'},M_{k'},n)$ with three identities. If $\mu:G\to G$ acts in coordinates by multiplication by the structural image of $c\in k$, then $e(H^n(\mu)x)=c e(x)$ for every $x$. The corresponding statement holds for each $c'\in k'$ and each $\mu':G'\to G'$ whose coordinates multiply by its structural image. Finally $e'(H^n(q)(j_H^*x))=B(e(x))$ for every $x\in H^n(G)$. No module action on $H^n(G)$ or $H^n(G')$ is assumed, and no flatness or tensor injectivity is asserted.

proof.text: Use the natural unit-module coordinates to construct the sectionwise isomorphisms G and Gprime to the lifted associated etale unit sheaves. On U the isomorphism sends x to ULift.up of the inverse unit coordinate applied to a_U(x). Naturality of both coordinate systems proves the sheaf-map equation. Compose their cohomology maps with the coefficient-universe, etale/Zariski and source-H comparisons. Transport the target unit through its module pullback isomorphism and the unique isomorphism of the displayed square with the categorical pullback.

Section coordinates determine scalar endomorphisms uniquely. The unit-coordinate multiplication formula identifies each such map with the lifted tensor pullback of multiplication by the global structural scalar. Naturality of the cohomology comparisons identifies its H-map with ordinary structural multiplication, giving both scalar identities.

Choose a finite affine cover and its inverse-image cover; all tuple intersections are affine. Under the constructed section isomorphisms the adjoint formula hq gives exactly the pullback coefficient map on each intersection. Use the affine Cech inverse-image comparison to identify its effect on cycle classes with the untensored canonical map B. Every class is represented by a cycle. Transport back from the categorical square to the displayed one. This does not use flatness or an invertible tensor comparison.
